### 2. get-di-registrations-default-response-exceeds-mcp-cap

| Field | Content |

| Diagnosis | Confirmed live at `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/AdvancedAnalysisTools.cs:66-100`. The `GetDiRegistrations` default path (`showLifetimeOverrides=false`, `summary=false`) serialises the entire registrations list at line 79 with no pagination or cap: `return JsonSerializer.Serialize(new { count = results.Count, registrations = results }, JsonDefaults.Indented)`. On a 141-registration DI graph this produces an 86 KB body that exceeds the MCP inline transport cap, causing the host to degrade to a write-to-disk envelope. The `summary=true` opt-in mode already exists, but is caller-opt-in. The `showLifetimeOverrides=true` path has the same structural problem at line 92-98. ### 4. symbol-refactor-preview-auto-applies-without-explicit-apply-call

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Status | pending |
| Backlog rows closed | `symbol-refactor-preview-auto-applies-without-explicit-apply-call` |
| Diagnosis | Root cause confirmed as hypothesis 1 (the preview-gate is broken — the service auto-applies). `SymbolRefactorService.PreviewAsync` at `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/SymbolRefactorService.cs:86` calls `_refactoringService.ApplyRefactoringAsync(stepPreview.PreviewToken, "symbol_refactor_preview", ct)` inside its chaining loop for every sub-operation. `ApplyRefactoringAsync` writes to disk via `PersistChangedDocumentsFromSolutionAsync` and calls `_changeTracker.RecordChange(workspaceId, description, appliedFiles, toolName)` at `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/RefactoringService.cs:342`. The `toolName` passed is the literal string `"symbol_refactor_preview"`, which is why `workspace_changes` shows seq 2+3 entries attributed to `symbol_refactor_preview` — they come from the inner apply calls, not from the outer composite redeem. The comment at lines 101-104 of `SymbolRefactorService.cs` explicitly acknowledges the design flaw: "each sub-op already wrote to disk via apply". Hypothesis 2 (ledger misattribution) is a symptom, not a separate failure mode. The fix must eliminate the inner `ApplyRefactoringAsync` calls — not patch the `toolName` string. |
| Approach | Fix is confined to `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/SymbolRefactorService.cs`. Rewrite `PreviewAsync` (lines 57-114) to chain sub-operations purely in-memory by threading `Solution` values rather than calling `ApplyRefactoringAsync` after each step. (1) Replace the inner `ApplyRefactoringAsync` call with a direct lookup of the sub-step's preview store entry via `_previewStore.Retrieve(stepPreview.PreviewToken)` to extract its `ModifiedSolution`. (2) Pass the accumulated `modifiedSolution` as input to the next sub-operation. Introduce a private overload of `ExecuteOperationAsync` that accepts an explicit `Solution` parameter (bypassing `_workspace.GetCurrentSolution`) and passes it to underlying Roslyn API calls (`Renamer.RenameSymbolAsync`, `EditService.PreviewMultiFileTextEditsAsync` both accept `Solution` directly). (3) After the loop, store the final accumulated `modifiedSolution` via `_previewStore.Store` as the composite token. (4) Call `_previewStore.Invalidate` on intermediate tokens to avoid store bloat. (5) Check whether `ICompositePreviewStore` (already injected) provides a direct solution-chaining primitive — use it if so. No changes to `RefactoringService`, `IPreviewStore`, `ChangeTracker`, or `SymbolRefactorTools.cs`. |
| Scope | Production files touched: 1 — `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/SymbolRefactorService.cs`. Test files: 1 — new test class `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/SymbolRefactorPreviewTests.cs` (or extend `RefactoringToolsIntegrationTests.cs`). |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 35000 |
| Risks | (1) The per-step `Execute*Async` helpers call into `_refactoringService`, `_editService`, `_restructureService` which each internally call `_workspace.GetCurrentSolution(workspaceId)` — the executor must audit whether each underlying service accepts an explicit `Solution` parameter or always reads from the live workspace. If any is hardwired, executor may need to add an overload in a second service file (still within Rule 3 if limited to 1-2 additional files, but needs verification at execution time).
